title: Print Log Analysis — ASP File Printed from Shared Workstation

lines.msg: Print job received: NCIA_ASP_2024.pdf (247 pages)
Job assigned to printer SEC-PRN-01 (Security Office)
Job status: Processing
Job completed: 247 pages printed successfully
Printer SEC-PRN-01: No user authentication recorded for this job
Job originated from workstation SECWS-02 (10.66.1.55) — No Active Directory login detected
Workstation SECWS-02 is not domain-joined and uses local account 'sec.office.shared'
SUSPICIOUS: ASP file (NCIA_ASP_2024.pdf) printed after hours, from unauthenticated workstation
File access timestamp matches Ray Delgado's last shift: 10/21/2026 10:47 PM
No user ID linked to print job; job logged under shared account 'sec.office.shared'
No record of print job review or approval
Job completed successfully; no errors detected

instructorNote: This inject confirms the timing and method of the ASP leak. The shared workstation (SECWS-02) was used, and no authentication was recorded — a critical gap. The legal team must decide if this constitutes a strong enough lead to involve law enforcement. IT must now explain why the workstation lacks authentication.
